# Codewhale agent guidance

Keep this file durable. Derive changing release, provider, branch, and flake
state from the repository, tests, CI, and current issue tracker rather than from
instructions or memory. The nearest scoped `AGENTS.md` adds path-specific rules.

## Working rules

- Inspect status and existing consumers before editing. Preserve unrelated,
  dirty, and untracked work.
- Prefer the simplest implementation that preserves observable contracts. A
  rewrite is acceptable when justified by product intent and observed behavior,
  not as a shortcut around understanding existing code.
- Search for behavior and symbols before reviving work from an old branch. If a
  lane is obsolete, preserve its intent and evidence rather than merging stale
  code mechanically.
- A small coherent change may be committed directly to `main` when that checkout
  is current, clean, and owns the affected files. A worktree remains the right
  safety boundary for conflicting, dirty, stale, or independent work. Local
  commit permission never implies push, merge, tag, release, or deploy permission.
- When the task is local-only, stay fully offline: no browsing, GitHub or remote
  Git operations, downloads, dependency installation, provider calls, or
  source/diff transmission. Record the missing external receipt and keep working
  locally.
- Public name is **Codewhale**. Compatibility identifiers such as `CodeWhale`,
  `codew`, protocol names, and storage keys change only through an explicit
  migration.
- Keep providers and models first-class and provider-neutral.
- Never rewrite published history, retag a release, force-push a shared ref, or
  publish without explicit authorization. Preserve human contributor credit.

## Current contracts

- The model-facing subagent tool is `agent`. Do not revive removed
  `agent_open`/`agent_eval`/`agent_close`/`delegate_to_agent` surfaces or parallel
  lifecycle/tag systems.
- `BASE_PROMPT` in `crates/tui/src/prompts/text.rs` is the sole base prompt.
- There is exactly one turn loop: `Engine::run_turn` in
  `crates/tui/src/core/engine/turn_loop.rs`. Note that `crates/tui/src/core/`
  is a module inside the TUI crate — it is not `crates/core`, which owns
  request construction, bounded fragments, and thread/session types and
  runs no turns. Do not add a second loop beside the one that exists; a
  guard test (`crates/core/tests/single_turn_loop.rs`) fails if you do.
- The system prompt + tool catalog are a session-pinned KV-cache prefix
  (`docs/CACHE.md`). Any new session-context contributor must state its
  KV-cache effect: frozen prefix vs. append-only history. Never splice a
  volatile fact into the prefix; append it as a user-role message.
- These active modules are repeatedly misidentified as dead; verify consumers
  before removal: `tui/src/context_budget.rs`, `tui/src/model_registry.rs`,
  `tui/src/prompt_zones.rs`, `tui/src/tools/remember.rs`, and
  `config/src/route/`. Native memory lives in `tui/src/native_memory.rs`;
  `tools/remember.rs` is its capture path.
- Environment-specific behavior belongs in `docs/ENVIRONMENTS.md`, not here.

## Code, migrations, and evidence

- Product intent and observed runtime behavior outrank a test's preferred
  implementation shape. Fix the product; do not contort production code to
  preserve a brittle assertion.
- Tests are selective evidence, not the specification. Do not add tests by
  default. Add or retain one when it cheaply protects a high-risk behavior such
  as safety, data integrity, protocol compatibility, or a reproduced regression.
- Rewrite or remove tests that duplicate coverage, freeze internals, overspecify
  copy or layout, preserve obsolete behavior, or cost more than the risk they
  cover. Never weaken real safety or data-integrity behavior merely to make a
  gate pass.
- Prefer focused compilation, a relevant existing check, and direct product or
  manual evidence. Run a broad suite only when the change creates a genuine
  cross-cutting or release risk. Do not repeatedly rerun an unchanged suite.
- Declared migrations are one-way. Once the repository adopts a replacement
  architecture or shared spine, new work uses it and touched legacy code moves
  toward it. Do not add another legacy call site for convenience. Keep a
  compatibility path only for an actual external contract, and label that
  boundary explicitly.

Useful commands, selected according to risk rather than run ritualistically:

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo test -p codewhale-config -p codewhale-protocol
cargo test --workspace
cargo build --release -p codewhale-cli -p codewhale-tui
```

`cargo nextest run` (config in `.config/nextest.toml`) is the fast way to
run an intentionally selected suite; `cargo test --no-run` can answer a compile
question without spending time executing unrelated cases, and `cargo test --doc`
covers doc examples when those examples changed.
`scripts/dev-test.sh <area>` maps a code area to its fastest `-p` invocation
and applies the portable isolated build-dir topology for new worktrees
(`scripts/dev-cache.sh`, `scripts/dev-cargo.sh`). See
`docs/BUILD_PERFORMANCE.md`.

Report commands actually run and distinguish source, local tests, packaged
artifacts, CI, and public release state. Describe the evidence actually needed
for the claim; a test count is not a proxy for product quality.

Community reports, PRs, logs, and reviews are evidence. Canonical human
identities come from `.github/AUTHOR_MAP`; `Co-authored-by` credit is for
humans and for recognized agent contributors (the exact identities listed in
`AGENT_CONTRIBUTOR_IDENTITIES` in `scripts/check-coauthor-trailers.py`, such as
`Codewhale Agent`); unknown bot/tool trailers are still rejected.
Leave unrelated work intact and keep new enforcement dry-run unless explicitly
approved.

git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
fix(credentials): parse the agy state.vscdb token envelope for sign-in

Antigravity 1.1.13 no longer stores a bare token under
`antigravityUnifiedStateSync.oauthToken`. The value is a base64 protobuf
envelope (marker message + inner base64 blob carrying the access token,
"Bearer", a refresh token, and an expiry), so the old bare-string parser
handed the whole blob back as if it were a credential and sign-in failed.

Parse both shapes the store actually carries. `antigravityAuthStatus` is
the row the app keeps current, so its JSON `apiKey` wins; the envelope is
the fallback and is honored only while its recorded expiry is still in
the future. An expired envelope reads as absent, not as an error — the
honest outcome is "sign in to Antigravity again", which is the same
read-only, never-refresh contract this module has always stated. Legacy
bare-string and JSON values still import through the original parser.

The refresh token is parsed past and dropped rather than retained: this
import never refreshes the external store, so holding the value would be
secret material kept for no purpose. No token material is logged, and
the tests build synthetic envelopes rather than using real fixtures.

SUMMARY:
 The composer has exactly one display-vs-buffer hook today — `App::composer_display_input()`/`composer_display_cursor()` (crates/tui/src/tui/app/composer.rs:574,578) — but it is a whole-buffer swap for history search, returns `&str`, and is bypassed by the mouse hit-testing path (crates/tui/src/tui/mouse_ui.rs:174,239 read raw `app.input`), so it is not a usable hook for a partial, per-line transform without adding an index map. Design A (render-only `[Image #N]`) is feasible but forces a display↔buffer char-index mapping through the composer's most fragile math: cursor row/col (widgets/mod.rs:4062, which documents a prior caret-desync regression), selection ranges (widgets/mod.rs:1504), mouse mapping, and atomic cursor motion. Design B (shorten the stored line) touches one producer (app.rs:5865), one parser (file_mention.rs:757), and ~18 tests — much lower risk — but the literal DOES live in persisted cross-version state (saved sessions re-read by backtrack, offline_queue.json, composer_history.txt, composer_stash.jsonl), and one consumer of the parser is the Runtime-Chat path-redaction guard, so the parser must keep accepting the legacy form rather than being renamed. Note also that design B as described still leaves the full path in the line, so it does not actually deliver Claude Code's compact token.

RECOMMENDATION:
 RECOMMENDATION: Design B is lower risk by a wide margin — but be clear with the user that **B as specified does not achieve the stated goal**. Dropping the description turns `[Attached image: 1920x1440 PNG (2.3MB) at /Users/x/Library/.../Screenshot 2026-08-24 at 10.31.22.png]` into `[Image #1: /Users/x/Library/.../Screenshot 2026-08-24 at 10.31.22.png]`. That removes ~28 characters, and the path — normally the longest part — is still there. Claude Code's compact `[Image #1]` is only reachable by hiding the path, i.e. design A or a side table.

RISK ORDER, concretely:
- B (rename + drop description): ~10 production lines + doc/test churn, zero index-space math. Lowest risk.
- A (render-only): no persistence risk at all, but it forces a display↔buffer index map through the single most fragile code in the composer.
- Side table (buffer holds `[Image #1]`, path in a map): lowest visual noise, highest risk — it is exactly what image_attach.rs:8 was written to refuse, and it breaks the four durability paths enumerated in the findings (backtrack, offline queue, stash, history recall).

concurrency:
  # PRs still share one group so a new push cancels the superseded head.
  # Push/schedule/dispatch on main must be keyed by SHA: with cancel-in-progress
  # false, GitHub still cancels a *pending* run in the same group when a new
  # one queues. That is how 31 of the last 40 main CI runs vanished without a
  # verdict (test bankruptcy, 2026-08-19). Each SHA gets its own group so
  # every commit on main actually finishes.
  group: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && format('ci-pr-{0}', github.event.pull_request.number) || format('ci-{0}-{1}', github.workflow, github.sha) }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

env:

  CARGO_INCREMENTAL: 0
  RUSTFLAGS: -Dwarnings

  # under load and aborted the whole lib suite (signal 6). 8 MiB is the
  # measured-safe floor; nextest's per-process runs are unaffected either way.
  RUST_MIN_STACK: 8388608

content.text:
Full CI is now running on my head — the first real verdict on this branch in a while. Here's where things stand.

## Landed, verified, pushed (3 commits)

**1. `76bba1231` — agy sign-in fix (the in-flight work).** Finished it. Two things the handoff claimed were clean were not: `cargo check` failed on a dead `refresh_token` field, and clippy failed on `unnecessary_lazy_evaluations`. A backgrounded clippy even reported **exit 0 with empty output** while the foreground run of the identical command failed — so that's a third false-green this cycle. I dropped the refresh token from the type entirely rather than `#[allow]`-ing it, which also makes the read-only contract structural: the value can't leak because there's no field to leak it from. Added 4 synthetic-envelope tests (no real token material). `16 passed` on the slice, `11188 passed; 0 failed` full suite.

**2. `a1e6e5386` — your spacing complaint.** Root-caused, and it's a real defect. Your `~/.codewhale/settings.toml` has `transcript_spacing = "compact"`, which you never chose — the `calm` preset wrote it. At compact, an `Activity` boundary spends **zero** rows, so reasoning → the tool it ran → the answer all fuse. `/config` even described calm as *"Quieter chrome and denser transcript"*.

I first tried making compact always breathe around answers — then found `compact_spacing_keeps_reasoning_and_answer_in_one_response_block`, a test asserting exactly the opposite on purpose. So I **reverted that** and fixed the actual bug instead: calm now selects `comfortable`, the description tells the truth, and a one-way flag-guarded migration lifts the stored calm+compact combination once. Compact still means what it always meant for anyone who picks it deliberately. `11190 passed; 0 failed`.

**3. `09b43038b` — a red CI gate nobody mentioned.** `check-readme-translations.py` is an unconditional CI leg and it has been **failing with 36 errors on every push** since `d070d510c` added `docs/AUTOMATION.md` to the README without touching the 18 translations. Fixed the link in all 18 using each language's own connector, restamped. Both gates now pass.

## Three claims in the handoff that were false

- **#5600 is fabricated.** It's a closed spam issue titled *"How Much Does Behavioral Health Medical Billing Cost in Texas?"* Zero commits anywhere. Nothing was fixed.
- **#5569 is Unix-only.** The hard-link guard is behind `#[cfg(unix)]`; Windows is explicitly unguarded.
- **#5568 is a no-op by default.** `sandbox_denied_read_paths` defaults empty, so out of the box the full-disk read in the issue still happens — but CHANGELOG claims it "bounds full-disk reads in any posture". That's an overclaim worth correcting before release.

## The buried lede — this reframes the release lane

**PR #5606 was merged to main yesterday at 23:52** (`3a50fdca2`). It carried a **rebased copy of 75 of this branch's commits**. Your local `origin/main` was stale, which made `rev-list` report "105 0" — falsely ahead-only. Real divergence: 106 ahead, 78 behind, and 75 of those 78 are duplicates. Only 2 commits on main are genuinely new.

So the instruction "take #5606 once he adds a Closes line" is moot — it's already in.

I probed the reconciliation in a throwaway worktree: **7 conflicted files, 14 hunks** — `CHANGELOG.md`, `crates/tui/CHANGELOG.md`, and the four mega-files I decomposed for #5586 (main has the pre-extraction versions). Not the ~75-file disaster the recon predicted. Tractable in one sitting. I aborted and removed the probe — I haven't merged anything.

## `[Image #1]` — the honest shape

The compact token is only reachable by hiding the path, and the path is the long part. Shortening the stored line gets you `[Image #1: /Users/.../Screenshot 2026-08-24 at 10.31.22.png]` — barely better.

Worth knowing: `sanitize_isolated_chat_attachments` redacts these lines so a managed-chat host never sees a local path, and it shares the parser with four stores that re-parse across restarts (sessions/backtrack, offline queue, composer history, stash). Changing the stored format risks that redaction failing open. The render-only approach has **zero** persistence or security exposure — it never changes stored text — at the cost of a display↔buffer index map through the composer's cursor/selection/mouse math. That's the right trade, and it's what I'll build next.

**Nothing released, tagged, bumped, or merged to main.** `Cargo.toml` is still `0.9.11`. I'll report the CI verdict when it lands, then start the composer work — say the word if you'd rather I take the main reconciliation or PR #5584 (draft, CI-green, `Closes #5543`, the cleanest merge available) first.

spend". `FleetUsageCeiling` (crates/protocol/src/fleet.rs:846) carries

expensive models and a run of cheap ones hit it at the same token count.

one. Commit b88462574 removed `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` from NVIDIA NIM's
credential fallback list, which had been silently sending a DeepSeek key
to NVIDIA's endpoint on provider switch. A reader deciding what to
rotate needed that direction stated, so it is now named explicitly.

CHAR indices, not bytes — every render/cursor/mouse consumer listed above is char-based (app.rs:611, widgets/mod.rs:4114 `char_idx`, mouse_ui.rs:197). Convert `MediaAttachmentReference.{start_byte,end_byte}` (the only byte-space input) to chars in the single forward pass that builds `text`.

Mapping rules (mirror composer.rs:769-780 exactly):
- `to_display(b)`: for each span, b <= buffer_start -> unshifted; b >= buffer_start+buffer_len -> shift by (display_len - buffer_len); strictly interior -> display_start.
- `to_buffer(d)`: inverse; interior of a token -> buffer_start.
- `to_display_floor(b)` / `to_display_ceil(b)`: interior -> display_start / display_start+display_len. Selection painting only (widgets/mod.rs:1505).

feat(tui): render composer attachments as a compact [Image #1] token

A pasted screenshot filled the composer with
`[Attached image: 1920x1440 PNG (2.3MB) at /var/folders/.../Screenshot
2026-08-24 at 10.31.22.png]` — most of a line of path for something the
user already knows they attached.

The obvious fix is to shorten the stored text, and it is the wrong one.
That line is deliberately path-bearing: it survives editing, history
recall, queueing and session reload with no side table, four persisted
stores round-trip it (saved sessions via backtrack, the offline queue,
composer history, the stash), and `sanitize_isolated_chat_attachments`
parses the same form to redact local paths before anything reaches a
managed Runtime Chat host. A format change risks that redaction failing
open on text restored from an older store.

So this is render-only. The buffer is untouched and every one of those
guarantees holds unchanged; only what is painted differs. `ComposerDisplay`
collapses each attachment line to `[Image #N]` (or `[Video #N]`) and
carries the mapping back to buffer coordinates, so the text, the caret,
the selection and mouse hit-testing all agree on one geometry.

Notes on the design:
- Numbering is positional and rebuilt each frame, so deleting attachment
  #1 of 3 renumbers the rest on the next paint. Nothing is written back,
  so there is no stale number to go wrong.
- Spans are sparse rather than a per-char index map: with no attachments
  the display borrows the buffer and allocates nothing, which is the
  overwhelmingly common frame.
- A history-search query is passed through uncollapsed; it is a query,
  not a buffer.
- The caret crosses a collapsed line in one step. Stepping through it
  grapheme by grapheme would look like a frozen cursor for the ~60
  characters the token hides.
- Selection edges floor and ceil, so a selection touching an attachment
  highlights the whole token rather than a fraction of it.

**Your two asks:**

I first tried making compact always breathe, then found `compact_spacing_keeps_reasoning_and_answer_in_one_response_block` asserting the opposite *on purpose* — so I reverted that and fixed the actual trap instead. - **`[Image #1]`** — `81a1afdac`. Changing the stored format risks that redaction failing open on text restored from an older store. So the buffer is untouched and only the paint changes. Caret crosses a token in one step; selection edges floor/ceil so a token highlights whole.

**CI was red and nobody knew** — the test legs had never run on this head. I dispatched a full run and got three real failures:

- **Safety gate** — **a genuine flake**, not a regression. I reproduced it locally twice in ~35 runs of the same filter. `RuntimeChatRelayHost::open` fails intermittently under parallel load. Same class as #5605. I have not fixed it — I'd be guessing at the mechanism, and I'd rather tell you that than ship a speculative fix.

**Contributor work:** `93e0ffd24` closes the new issue **#5607** from @diegovskytl — OpenCode Go is a gateway whose roster is whatever the key unlocks, but the catalog refresh was gated on a hard-coded pair of providers. All the plumbing already existed. I replaced the `matches!` with a named rule so the next gateway doesn't get forgotten.

The one that mattered: #5588 said "NVIDIA credentials no longer leak into the DeepSeek keychain" but the actual fix removed `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` from NVIDIA NIM's fallback list — a **DeepSeek** key was being sent to NVIDIA. READ-ONLY investigation in the Codewhale repo at ${REPO}, branch codex/v0912-integration-20260823.

ABSOLUTE RULES:
- Do NOT edit, create, or delete ANY file. No git writes. No cargo fmt --all. Read/grep only.

Your final text IS the return value. Be dense and concrete. Prioritise DEFECTS over inventory.

const OUT = {

  additionalProperties: false,
  required: ['summary', 'findings', 'recommendation', 'risks'],
  properties: {
    summary: { type: 'string' },
    findings: {

}

phase('Audit')

const tasks = [

    label: 'model-facts-audit',
    prompt: `${RULES}

TASK: Find CONCRETE ERRORS in Codewhale's hard-coded model facts. The user says the categorization is "sketchy" — your job is to produce a list of specific wrong entries, not a tour.

WHERE TO LOOK (verify these paths exist, correct any drift):
- crates/tui/src/models.rs — context_window_for_model() and friends; lots of hard-coded per-model numbers with comments citing dates.
- crates/tui/src/model_registry.rs
- crates/tui/src/model_profile.rs
- crates/tui/src/pricing.rs — per-model pricing / billing surfaces.
- crates/config/src/provider_templates.rs — per-provider default_model and models lists.
- crates/tui/src/models_dev_live.rs and crates/tui/src/provider_lake.rs — the live Models.dev catalog that is supposed to override the bundled numbers.

DELIVER:
1. The full inventory of DIMENSIONS along which a model is categorized (context window, vision/modality, tool-call support, reasoning support, tier/class, pricing, default-ness, aliases). For each: where it is stored, and whether it is bundled-static, live-fetched, or both.
2. THE MAIN DELIVERABLE — a list of specific entries that look WRONG or STALE. Look hard for:
   - Models whose bundled context window contradicts the comment above it, or contradicts the same model's entry elsewhere in the repo.
   - The SAME model appearing under two providers with DIFFERENT facts (context window, pricing, capability). This is the highest-value class of bug — report every instance you find.
   - Capability flags asserted for a model family rather than a model (e.g. all of provider X marked vision-capable because one model is).
   - Alias tables mapping a slug to the wrong canonical model.
   - Comments citing a date (e.g. "as of 2026-08-08") that are now stale relative to the repo's current date of 2026-08-25, especially where a newer model exists in the same table.
   - Defaults pointing at a model the provider does not actually serve (there is precedent: the openai provider once defaulted to deepseek-v4-pro).
3. Where the bundled value and the live Models.dev value disagree, state which one wins at runtime and whether the bundled one can ever shadow a correct live one.
4. Rank your findings by user-visible harm: a wrong context window causes premature or missed compaction; wrong pricing causes wrong cost display; a wrong capability flag causes a hard request failure.

Return the structured object. Put the ranked defect list in 'findings' and the fix order in 'recommendation'.`,
  },
  {
    label: 'fleet-roles-in-picker',
    prompt: `${RULES}

TASK: The user wants the provider/model screen to surface WHAT A MODEL IS FOR — specifically "what fleet roles exist for certain models". Work out what data already exists to support that, and design the smallest honest version.

INVESTIGATE:
1. What IS a fleet role in this codebase? Find the role taxonomy. Look at crates/tui/src/fleet/, crates/protocol/src/fleet.rs, and anything about "role posture" (issue #5575 says role posture has no single source of truth — find out whether that is still true and where the candidate sources are).
2. Is there any existing mapping from a model (or model capability) to a role, or a recommended-model-per-role? Or is role assignment purely user-configured? Be precise — this determines whether the feature is "surface existing data" or "invent new data".
3. Where would it render? Read crates/tui/src/tui/provider_picker.rs (~8400 lines): find the row-rendering function, the detail/side panel for a selected provider, and what per-model info is shown TODAY when a user browses models (there is a models stage — find it, look for MessageId::PickerActionModels).
4. Assess the "Artificial Analysis" idea. Codewhale already integrates models.dev via crates/tui/src/models_dev_live.rs with a disk cache and background refresh. Report how that integration works (fetch, cache path, refresh cadence, failure behavior, and crucially its KV-cache/offline implications per docs/CACHE.md and the AGENTS.md offline rule). Then say whether an Artificial Analysis-style quality/speed/price index could ride the SAME mechanism, and what it would cost. Flag honestly if adding a second external data source conflicts with the project's offline-first and footprint goals — the standing product goal is "fast, slim, easy to run".
5. Propose the SMALLEST change that makes the model list genuinely more informative using data Codewhale ALREADY has locally (no new network dependency). Be concrete about which fields and which render site.

Return the structured object.`,
  },

    label: 'provider-screen-neutrality',
    prompt: `${RULES}

TASK: The user just had a per-provider hotkey removed from the provider picker (a dedicated "S = SenseNova" button that stole a letter from the advertised a-z jump). Find the REST of the arbitrary per-provider special-casing in the provider/model UI, so we can judge what else should go.

INVESTIGATE crates/tui/src/tui/provider_picker.rs (~8400 lines) and crates/tui/src/tui/views/:
1. Enumerate EVERY place the picker branches on a specific ApiProvider variant or a specific template id. For each, classify it as:

   (b) ARBITRARY — a convenience shortcut, a hand-picked ordering, or a hard-coded label that any provider could equally claim.
   Give file:line and a one-line justification for the classification. Be rigorous: do not call something arbitrary just because it names a provider.
2. Specifically list the remaining top-level single-letter hotkeys in the picker's key handler and which are provider-specific vs categorical. Note which ones collide with the a-z type-ahead jump the footer advertises.
3. Look at the action-bar footers (search ActionHint::new) and report whether the hint set is getting overcrowded — count the hints in each footer variant.
4. Report the provider ORDERING logic: is the row order alphabetical, hand-curated, or tiered? If hand-curated, where is the list and does it privilege particular providers without stating why?
5. Cross-check against issue #5588 (provider neutrality: DeepSeek-exclusive gates). Report which of the gates you found overlap with what #5588 already tracks, so we do not double-file.

Return the structured object. Put the (a)/(b) classified list in 'findings' and a recommended removal order in 'recommendation'.`,
  },
]

content.text:
SenseNova's gone. Here's where things stand while the categorization audit runs.

## The SenseNova button — it wasn't just clutter

You were right that there's no reason for it, and it turned out to be an actual bug rather than a cosmetic one.

`S` had a dedicated key handler *and* its own `ActionHint` button in both footer variants. It's one of four compatible templates — `opencode-zen`, `opencode-go`, `sensenova`, `agnes` — and the only one with a button. `P` already opens the list containing all of them.

The real problem: the wide footer advertises **`a-z` jump**, and the `S` arm sat ahead of the type-ahead arm with the same guard the `A` handler documents. So typing `s` couldn't jump to SenseNova, SiliconFlow, Stepfun, or SGLang. One provider's shortcut broke the advertised behavior for every provider starting with that letter. Removing it hands the letter back.

I also found `ProviderCustomFormHint` literally said *"SenseNova: S"* — now false. That string lives in 15 locales, and locale **parity** would have stayed green the whole time because the keys never changed, only the meaning. So I fixed the text in all 14 translations too rather than leaving it wrong in every language but English.

The keyboard test that existed only to pin `S` is rewritten to walk the template list, so it now covers the path every other template uses and keeps its "a preset must not render as a blank custom form" assertion. `90d878442`, 11204 passed / 0 failed.

## CI is fully green

## What actually happened

My first commit this session (`76bba1231`) added an envelope parser, 16 passing tests, full suite green. But the tests built their fixture from the handoff's *written description* of the format rather than from the format itself. So they proved the parser could read its own fixture. Nothing more.

1. **Wrong base64 alphabet.** Your store writes *standard* base64 — padded, using `+`. My decoder only tried the two URL-safe alphabets, which reject `+`. The outer value never decoded at all. My own Python exploration hid this, because `urlsafe_b64decode` translates `-_`→`+/` and accepts both.

2. **Wrong nesting.** The real layout wraps each sentinel and its payload in a nested entry message; I'd assumed they were sibling fields, then unwrapped one level too many on top of that.

Fixed both, `169727b27`. Verified through the production code path against your actual store:

```

PARSED | access_len=260 | ya29=true | leaked_refresh=false | expires_at=1776009331
```

The `leaked_refresh=false` is the read-only contract holding in practice rather than by construction. No token material was printed or kept; the probe and the captured value are both deleted.

**Your envelope token expired 2026-04-12** — four months ago. Sign-in works today because the `antigravityAuthStatus` `apiKey` wins and *is* live. So the envelope path was pure fallback, which is exactly why nobody noticed it was broken.

I also made it **fail closed**: a value carrying the sentinel is recognisably an envelope, so when it won't parse the credential is now absent. Previously it fell through to the legacy bare-token reader, which handed back the entire 1068-character base64 blob as a bearer token — that *was* the original sign-in bug, not a recovery from it.

11205 passed, 0 failed. I didn't need computer-use — reading the SQLite store directly was more precise than driving the UI would have been.

- **`deepseek-reasoner` means different models on different providers** — V4-**Pro** on SiliconFlow, V4-**Flash** on seven others. 3× price difference (1.32 vs 0.44 /1M), silently.
- **Codex route compacts at 102,400 tokens** on a route whose real window is 400K–1.05M. A provider-level `128_000` override ignores the model entirely — so 3–8× premature compaction.
- **Every Gemini model is marked non-reasoning in the TUI**, including the Google default, while `crates/agent` says the opposite for the same ids.
- **`k3` and `moonshotai/kimi-k3` return non-reasoning** while `kimi-k3` returns reasoning — same product, so `reasoning_content` leaks into answer prose on those routes.
- **`claude-opus-5` is missing** from the server-side web-search table, and `claude-mythos-5` appears there and *nowhere else in the repo*.
- **A data-entry bug models.rs documents as fixed is still live** in the bundled JSON (`output: 262140`, a typo of the context window).

Root cause is structural: there are **two disconnected fact stacks**, and live Models.dev data never reaches the one that drives compaction and cost. So a model can show "256K out" on a Fleet badge and be budgeted at 32K by the engine.

the SiliconFlow V4-Pro row and on the V4-Flash row of seven other
providers. One alias meant two tiers depending on which provider was
active, at roughly 3x the input price, with nothing shown to the user.
They now mean Flash everywhere, matching every provider but the one.

models.rs: the reasoning table had no Gemini arm at all, so every Gemini
id — including `gemini-3.1-pro-preview`, which is DEFAULT_GOOGLE_MODEL —
reported non-reasoning while `crates/agent` reported the opposite for the
same id. The arm added here matches that registry exactly, including
leaving `gemini-3.5-flash-lite` false. The `kimi-` prefix test also
missed the provider-qualified `moonshotai/kimi-k3` and
`opencode-go/kimi-k3`, which the context-window table already treats as
the same product.

Bare `k3` is deliberately NOT included, and the audit that flagged it was
wrong. Its reasoning semantics are route-scoped — reasoning on the Kimi
Code host, not the direct Moonshot host — and a model-id-only function
cannot answer that. Adding it broke four tests that exist to pin exactly
that scoping; the route-aware pair in client/chat.rs owns the decision.

config.rs: the Codex arm returned OPENAI_CODEX_EFFECTIVE_CONTEXT_WINDOW_
TOKENS for every model, though the constant documents itself as a
"conservative offline floor for an OAuth model absent from a fresh Codex
roster". `gpt-5.6` is the Codex default and has a documented 1,050,000
window, so it was budgeted at 128,000 and compacted more than eight times
earlier than needed. The floor now applies only to the case it describes.
`max_output: Some(4096)` on that route is left alone: its comment states
it is a deliberate product decision, not a fallback.

diverge again.

OpenAI is beginning a limited preview of the GPT-5.6 series: Sol, the flagship model; Terra, a balanced model for everyday work; and Luna, a fast and affordable model.
